title: Send a message
summary: Trace an order notification across the campus network.

scenario.briefing: A customer placed an order, but the delivery notification never arrived. Trace the message path from the laptop to the messaging service to find where the route belongs.

objectives.description: Distinguish a request from a response.
Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: A laptop does not reach the API directly over the network. Start with the wireless link.
The campus wireless connects to the router, then to the orders API.
The API hands the notification to the messaging service.
The correct route is laptop, campus wifi, router, orders API, messaging service.

misconceptions.description: Jumping directly from the laptop to the API.
misconceptions.feedback: On this campus the wireless link reaches the router first. The router forwards traffic to the service network.

misconceptions.description: Confusing the reply with the original request.
misconceptions.feedback: The POST that creates the order is the request. The confirmation returned afterwards is the response.

sections.title: Networks move messages in hops
sections.body: A request travels through several devices. Wireless access, routers, and service endpoints each forward data toward its destination. A fault at any hop can stop the message even when the application code is fine.

sections.title: Requests and responses
sections.body: A client sends a request and a server returns a response. The request names an action and a target; the response reports an outcome and often carries data. Later you will use HTTP, the protocol that gives these messages a standard shape.

vocabulary.definition: The system that sends a request.
The system that receives and answers a request.
A small unit of data moved across a network.

steps.title: Trace the notification
steps.prompt: Click the devices in order from the laptop to the messaging service.
steps.explanation: The laptop reaches the wireless access point, the router forwards the request to the API, and the API calls the messaging service.

steps.title: Which message is which?
steps.prompt: The laptop sends an order to the API. The API replies with a confirmation number. Which part is the request?

options.label: The confirmation number returned by the API
The order data sent by the laptop to the API
The database lookup performed by the API

quiz.explanation: The laptop initiates the interaction by sending the order data. The confirmation is the response.

hints: Which message asks the server to do something?
The order data travels from the client to the server.
The request is the order data sent by the laptop.

steps.title: Network responsibility
steps.prompt: Select the accurate statements about networked systems.

statements.label: A message may pass through devices that do not understand the application data.
A network request is identical to a local function call.
A request can fail or time out, so the client must handle that outcome.
A successful send guarantees the server processed the request.

steps.explanation: Remote calls cross failure boundaries. A message being sent is not proof that the remote action succeeded.

accessibility.summary: Network nodes are buttons in a labeled diagram; a text list offers the same order selection.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use Tab to move between nodes and Enter to add a node to the route. Clear the route with the reset button.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each node announces its name, type, and whether it is connected. The selected route is read as an ordered list.
